description: Gripper version 1.20 (next after 1.19, builds on 1.19 / voice-13bdab11). The gripper should have a hook at both the bottom AND the top along the flat face, so the handle piece slides in and is held by both hooks. Bump to 1.20 per AGENTS.md versioning.

results.identified_issue: Read 'flat face' as the finger's straight outer edge (2.3's rail, rail_p), where Gen 9's base J-hook already sits; 'top' = toward the tip. Top hook = trace_photo.py top_hook(): the base hook run (PATCHES[1]) in rail (u,w), mirrored about u=8.5, plus a 2-point ramp back to the edge, spliced into the outline like the other patches, so concept.json/web get it free. Opposing hooks mean a rigid handle can only enter along Y; that's the interpretation, disclosed. If Jake meant a handle that drops in along the edge, one hook must open the other way or the handle must flex/snap. Handle blank lives in the 1.x version despite 'gripper only' because the request is about the handle fitting; it's a plain fit blank. RDP_SPLIT pins trace()'s rdp split to 1.19's len(Q)//2 point: letting it move re-picked beak vertices and the 15 deg viewer STL went non-manifold (3 bad edges near z 119). check_gripper_closure.py 'never touches' FAIL is pre-existing on every gen 15+ version, not this change.
results.summary: Version 1.20 adds a second hook at the top of the flat outer face, a mirror of the base hook. A black handle blank slides in sideways between the two hooks and is held by both.
results.detailed_description:
1.20 is 1.19 with a hook at both ends of the flat outer face. I copied the bottom J-hook, flipped it end for end, and put it at the top of the same straight edge, so the two notches face each other. Their floors are 39.8 mm apart. The rest of the finger is unchanged from 1.19.

I also added a handle blank to show the fit. It's a black plate 3.5 mm thick and as tall as the finger is thick (12 mm), with a foot shaped to fill each notch at 0.2 mm clearance. It has no strap slots, since the 1.x line is gripper only and the strap handle is 2.x.

Because the hooks face each other, a stiff handle can't slide in along the edge. It slides in sideways instead, across the finger's thickness from either face, until it's flush. Once it's in, the notch floors stop it moving along the edge, and both prongs stop it pulling outward: 0.3 mm of outward movement already catches on both. Only friction keeps it from sliding back out the side it came in. A detent or a stop on one face would fix that, if you want one.

All of 1.19's checks pass, plus new ones: the seated blank clears the finger, slides out without touching, and runs into the hooks if pushed. It still has 33 through-holes. Nothing has been printed. Have a look at the hooks, handle_in and handle_sliding previews.

summary: The gripper model needs a new version 1.20, built on 1.19, with a hook at both the bottom and top of the flat face. The handle piece should slide in and be held by both hooks, with the version bumped per AGENTS.md.
